actions.joint_pos.joint_names: Decision D1. The same 29 joints main selects with a lone '.*', named explicitly so that preserve_order has something to order by: preserve_order sorts a selection by the patterns it was given, so one pattern would leave PhysX's breadth-first order in place and the flag would do nothing. Naming them puts the action axis in the canonical depth-first order, which is the order mjlab produces, so an action vector means the same thing on both engines. Same joints, deliberately different index assignment; the content is pinned by tests/test_parity_static.py.
actions.joint_pos.preserve_order: Decision D1, and only meaningful together with the explicit joint_names above. Main leaves it False and accepts PhysX's breadth-first order, which no other engine reproduces.
actions.joint_pos.scale: Same 29 numbers, keyed per joint instead of by the sixteen actuator-group patterns main inherits from the Isaac Lab asset module. Taken from RobotSpec.joint_properties so the task needs no engine import; verified equal for every joint.
curriculum: Main declares an empty container; the task declares no curriculum terms.

observations.critic.joint_pos.params.ass: Decision D1. Main passes no asset_cfg, so the term reads the whole joint axis in the engine's own order -- PhysX's breadth-first walk on Isaac Sim, the model file's order on mjlab, which are not the same permutation. Naming all 29 joints with preserve_order puts the observation in the canonical depth-first order on both engines, matching the action axis. Same joints and same values, permuted; pinning only the action axis would leave a policy whose inputs and outputs are indexed differently per engine. The resolved order is pinned by tests/test_parity_static.py.
